posts.title: NSBP / NSHP day two
posts.description: I missed day one of the NSBP / NSHP Meeting in Raleigh NC . Day two was amazing; way too much to say in one post. posts.title: hacking on early LSST data
posts.description: After Scialog , Jackie Faherty (AMNH) and I organized a two-day hacking meeting in Tucson themed around the new LSST data (Data Preview 2) with Scialog participants and some of their students. I learned a ton! I learned how to use the LSST data. I built a robust (robust in the technical sense) multi-band periodogram. I learned that weak lensing tools are extremely mature these days. posts.title: generalizing searches for new physics
posts.description: I spent a great three days in Tucson working on the RCSA project called Scialog , which supports the funding and networks of early-career faculty (and faculty equivalents) in astrophysics. The events are built around open-ended discussions. In one of these we were discussing dark matter. I was going off about looking for dark matter in all observable channels, not just channels suggested by theory
